title: Hepatic Lipidosis
desc: L-carnitine, Taurine, Water-soluble vitamins, Thiamine, Vitamin B12 (cobalamin), Zinc, Vitamin E, SAMe, N-acetylcysteine, Fish oil

meds.name: Vitamin E
meds.doseText: 100-200 IU/day alpha tocopherol acetate per os

meds.name: N-acetylcysteine
freqs: IV BID until enteral feeding is established

notes: Do not feed a diet low in protein.
Check for bleeding tendencies (low vitamin K) before placing esophagostomy tube or PEG tube.
Avoid lactate and dextrose containing fluids.
Potassium and phosphorus supplementation as needed. Be aware of hypophospatemia subsequent to refeeding.
Water soluble vitamins: two-fold normal maintenance dose daily
Thiamine if ventroflexion (100-200 mg/day for 3 days)
Vitamin E 100-200 IU/day alpha tocopherol acetate per os
SAMe as a glutathione source (200 mg/day) or n-acetylcysteine (140 mg/kg IV as a loading dose than 70 mg/kg IV BID until enteral feeding established).
Fish Oil: 2000 mg/day supplies omega 3-poylunsaturated faty acids which are anti-inflammatory if the primary process is inflammatory.
Dr. Center has seen an increased survival rate in the treatment of HL from 62.5% to 85.3% with the addition of l-carnitine to her treatment protocol.
